quizzes.title: Forming the Government and the Council of Ministers
quizzes.passage: Appointing a Prime Minister is one of the first steps in forming a government in India. The Constitution says the President makes the appointment, but the President does not have complete freedom in the selection. In ordinary circumstances, the President invites the leader of the party that holds a majority in the Lok Sabha. If no single party has a clear majority, the President has to decide whom to invite by judging who is likely to win the confidence of the House. The Prime Minister holds office during the pleasure of the President. The Prime Minister leads a team of ministers known as the Council of Ministers. This team includes Cabinet Ministers, who are senior members placed below the Prime Minister, along with Ministers of State and Deputy Ministers. Each group has its own role in running government departments. Ministers may sit in Parliament or be appointed from outside it for a limited period. Ministers of State are one of the categories within this team, and the booklet describes their roles in detail. Taken together, these arrangements explain how the executive is formed, how the Prime Minister's position is structured, and how ministers take part in the work of Parliament.

questions.q: When no single party has a clear majority, the President invites a person who can command support of how many parties?
options: One party alone, the largest in the Lok Sabha
Two or more parties that together form a Lok Sabha majority
A coalition of Rajya Sabha members only
The party with the most seats in the previous government
questions.explanation: The booklet says the person invited should command support of two or more parties that make up a Lok Sabha majority.

questions.q: According to the booklet, which key ministries are overseen by Cabinet Ministers?
questions.explanation: The booklet names Home Affairs, Finance and Defence as key ministries overseen by Cabinet Ministers.

questions.q: In the booklet's list of the Prime Minister's key functions, the PM is described as Chairperson of which body?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the Prime Minister as Chairperson of the Union Cabinet among the key functions.

questions.q: Which category of ministers is described as operating independently, without oversight from Cabinet Ministers or Council of Ministers members?
options: Ministers of State assisting Cabinet Ministers
questions.explanation: The booklet describes MoS (IC) as operating independently, without oversight from Cabinet Ministers or Council of Ministers members.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Cabinet Ministers are senior members of the Council of Ministers placed below the Prime Minister.
Reason (R): Ministers of State are senior to Cabinet Ministers in the Council of Ministers.
Which one of the following is correct?
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: A matches the booklet's description of Cabinet Ministers, but the booklet describes Ministers of State as junior to Cabinet Ministers, so R is false.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Prime Minister is the Head of the Union Government and Leader of the Council of Ministers.
II. The President can dismiss the Prime Minister at any time.
III. A member of the Rajya Sabha can never be made Prime Minister.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement I matches the booklet, while II and III contradict its statements that the President cannot dismiss at any time and that Rajya Sabha members have been made PM.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. Deputy Ministers assist Cabinet Ministers or Ministers of State with administrative, political and parliamentary duties.
II. The Prime Minister's term is fixed at five years by the Constitution.
III. The Prime Minister is the Head of the Executive.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while II is wrong because the booklet says the Constitution does not fix the PM's term.

quizzes.title: Ministers and Appointment Rules
quizzes.passage: The Constitution provides for the appointment of the Prime Minister by the President, but the President's choice is shaped by the political situation in the Lok Sabha. Normally, the leader of the majority party is invited to form the government. When no party has a clear majority, the President looks for a person who can attract support from a combination of parties. The Prime Minister heads the government and guides its policy. Ministers are then chosen to help run the government, and the booklet lists several categories among them. Some ministers hold independent charge of ministries, while others assist senior ministers in their work. A minister who is not a member of Parliament has a limited time to become one. The booklet also notes that ministers may take part in the proceedings of both Houses without a guaranteed right to vote. The size of the council is restricted by a constitutional amendment, and the salary of the Prime Minister is set by law. Constitutional provisions on these matters are set out in several Articles, which the booklet links to each rule. The booklet also describes the Prime Minister as the head of the executive and the leader of the Council of Ministers. Together, these points give a basic picture of how the executive functions at the Union level.

questions.q: What is the minimum number of parties that the person invited by the President must be able to command support of, when no single party has a clear majority? (number)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the invited person should command support of two or more parties that make up a Lok Sabha majority.

questions.q: Which group of ministers assists Cabinet Ministers or Ministers of State with administrative, political and parliamentary duties?
questions.explanation: The booklet says Deputy Ministers assist cabinet ministers or MoS with administrative, political and parliamentary duties.

questions.q: Which category of ministers operates independently, without oversight from Cabinet Ministers? Give the abbreviation used in the booklet.
questions.explanation: The booklet abbreviates Ministers of State (Independent Charge) as MoS (IC).

questions.q: Which Union body does the Prime Minister chair, according to the booklet's key functions? (name of body)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the Prime Minister as Chairperson of the Union Cabinet.

questions.q: Name the first key ministry the booklet lists among those overseen by Cabinet Ministers.
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Home Affairs first among the key ministries overseen by Cabinet Ministers, followed by Finance and Defence.

questions.q: Which group of ministers is described as senior members of the Council of Ministers, placed below the Prime Minister?
questions.explanation: The booklet describes Cabinet Ministers as senior Council of Ministers members placed below the Prime Minister.

questions.q: Which house of Parliament has had a member made Prime Minister in some cases? (name of house)
questions.explanation: The booklet notes that there have been cases when a Member of the Rajya Sabha was made Prime Minister.

quizzes.title: Modi's Records and Prime Ministerial Firsts
quizzes.passage: Narendra Modi became India's longest continuously serving elected Prime Minister after completing 4,399 consecutive days in office. He had taken office on 26 May 2014, and this period surpassed the uninterrupted record held by Jawaharlal Nehru. The booklet explains that Nehru's overall tenure as Prime Minister lasted about 6,131 days, but that this total includes time when he served as head of an interim government before the first general elections. The Lok Sabha has 543 seats, and the party or alliance that commands a majority is normally called upon to form the government. Several Prime Ministers of India are noted for records that the booklet describes in short facts. These facts include the age at which a Prime Minister took office, the years in which the Prime Minister served, and the house of Parliament from which a Prime Minister came. Modi's record is described in the context of the country's general elections, and the booklet measures it in days rather than years. The booklet also notes that Nehru was the first Prime Minister of India and the first to die in office. Taken together, these facts give a useful picture of how the record of India's Prime Ministers can be compared.

questions.q: Which PM is described as the first Indian Prime Minister born after 15 August 1947?
questions.explanation: The booklet calls Narendra Modi the first Indian PM born after 15 August 1947.

questions.q: How many of the 543 Lok Sabha seats did the BJP-led NDA win in 2014?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the BJP-led NDA got an absolute majority of 336 out of 543 Lok Sabha seats in 2014.

questions.q: Which PM is described as India's 2nd PM of South Indian origin, from Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists HD Deve Gowda as India's 2nd PM of South Indian origin, from Karnataka.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The 2014 government is described as the first Non-Congress single party majority government.
Reason (R): The BJP itself became the first party since 1984 to get a majority in the Lok Sabha.
Which one of the following is correct?
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements appear in the booklet, and the BJP's own majority is the reason the 2014 government counts as a single party majority government.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Morarji Desai   ->   B. PM with the shortest tenure (16 days)
II. Rajiv Gandhi   ->   D. First PM to leave office after a no-confidence vote
III. V.P. Singh   ->   A. Youngest PM at 40 years
IV. Atal Bihari Vajpayee   ->   C. First Non-Congress PM
questions.explanation: Morarji Desai was the first Non-Congress PM, Rajiv Gandhi the youngest at 40, V.P. Singh the first to leave after a no-confidence vote, and Vajpayee had the shortest tenure.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Modi is among the few Indian PMs to secure 3 consecutive electoral mandates at the Union level.
II. Morarji Desai was India's youngest PM.
III. Atal Bihari Vajpayee's tenure was the longest of any PM.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement I matches the booklet, while II is wrong because Rajiv Gandhi was the youngest PM and III is wrong because Vajpayee had the shortest tenure.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. Rajiv Gandhi was India's youngest PM, at 40 years.
II. Gulzarilal Nanda was the only man to have twice served as Acting Prime Minister of India.
III. Morarji Desai was born in the 20th century.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while III is wrong because the booklet says Morarji Desai was the 2nd and last PM born in the 19th century.

quizzes.title: Modi's Records in Context
quizzes.passage: Narendra Modi has been Prime Minister since 26 May 2014, and his uninterrupted service has drawn attention in the booklet. The booklet also places him in a wider context of Prime Ministers who came from different backgrounds. Some of them took office at a young age, while others were very old when they became Prime Minister. A few Prime Ministers left office in unusual ways, and some held the post for only a very short time. The Lok Sabha has 543 seats, and the booklet records how many of those seats the 2014 alliance won. Several Prime Ministers also came from South India, and their origins are noted in the booklet. The booklet presents these details in short factual notes, which makes it possible to compare the careers of different leaders. The booklet also records that Jawaharlal Nehru was India's first Prime Minister and that Lal Bahadur Shastri was the second to die in office. Its notes on Nehru also mention that his overall tenure is recorded as about 6,131 days, including his period as interim Prime Minister before the first general elections. Taken together, the examples show the range of experience among India's Prime Ministers and the variety of paths they followed to office.

questions.q: In the 2014 Lok Sabha election, how many seats did the BJP-led NDA win? (number of seats, out of 543)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the BJP-led NDA got an absolute majority of 336 out of 543 Lok Sabha seats.

questions.q: The booklet describes Modi as the first Indian PM born after which date? (full date)
questions.explanation: The booklet calls Modi the first Indian PM born after 15 Aug 1947.

questions.q: Which PM is described in the booklet as India's youngest PM, at 40 years? (full name)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes Rajiv Gandhi as India's youngest Prime Minister at 40 years.

questions.q: At what age, in years, is the booklet's oldest Prime Minister, Morarji Desai, described as being?
questions.explanation: The booklet describes Morarji Desai as India's oldest Prime Minister at 81 years.

questions.q: Which PM is described in the booklet as the first PM to leave office following a no-confidence vote? (full name, initials allowed)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes V.P. Singh as the first PM to leave following a no-confidence vote.

questions.q: How many days was the tenure of the PM the booklet describes as having the shortest tenure? (number of days)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes Atal Bihari Vajpayee as the PM with the shortest tenure, of 16 days.

questions.q: Which PM is described in the booklet as India's 2nd PM of South Indian origin, from Karnataka? (full name)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists HD Deve Gowda as India's 2nd PM of South Indian origin, from Karnataka.
